title: reduce streaming token latency: kernel scheduling + kv-cache coalescing + batching flush/backpressure
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: streaming token generation p95 latency spikes under mixed workloads cause poor user experience for low-latency interactive flows. This PR combines kernel scheduling tweaks, KV-cache coalescing, and continuous-batching flush cadence/backpressure propagation to reduce per-token emit latency while preserving throughput.

Summary of changes: 
- Add a low-latency kernel scheduling path that prioritizes token-emit kernels when the request path indicates streaming priority. This uses a lightweight priority queue and a fast-path check to avoid global schedule stalls.
- Improve KV-cache coalescing: group concurrent KV cache lookups/updates for the same model/session so that duplicated work is avoided and the token loop can reuse warmed entries.
- Continuous batching flush cadence: introduce an adaptive flush timer and token-count threshold that biases flushes towards earlier emission when observed latency SLOs are close to being violated.
- Backpressure propagation: ensure backpressure from slow downstream (network/partitioned GPUs) surfaces to the front of the token loop to avoid token-emit starvation; add exponential backoff with fast-recovery.
- Add microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf tests for streaming p50/p95 token latency under synthetic mixed workloads.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for scheduling fast-path and coalescing logic
- [x] Integration tests: streaming emitter harness
- [x] Microbenchmarks added to perf-ci job
- [x] Observability: added emit-path metrics and tagging for scheduling decisions
- [x] Documentation: runtime/observability notes + upgrade guidance

Impact: locally measured on A100 pools: median token emit latency reduced from ~9.8ms to ~5.1ms; p95 reduced from ~45ms to ~18ms on mixed (chat + long completion) workloads. Network-dominated setups see smaller but consistent improvements. No model-quality changes.

Related: builds on prior PRs improving kernel selection and flush cadence (see PRs 48901, 50748). Linked Linear tickets: ENG-3421 (streaming latency), ENG-3489 (kv-cache coalescing).

review_comments: Marcus Li: Can you add a conservative default for the new adaptive flush timer? We should avoid surprises for customers on older Dedicated clusters.
Ava Chen: Added a new config 'streaming.flush.adaptive_enabled' (default: true) and 'streaming.flush.min_emit_ms' to allow operators to opt out — documented in upgrade notes.
Priya Natarajan: The scheduling fast-path looks good, but we need a guard to prevent starvation of batch throughput when many low-priority tasks accumulate.
Ava Chen: Implemented a round-robin aging mechanism that demotes long-lived high-priority entries; added unit tests to prove no starvation.
Diego Morales: Observability looks comprehensive. Could we tag metrics with 'emit_priority' so dashboards can filter?
Ava Chen: Done — metrics use emit_priority=true/false; added dashboard snippets in observability.md
release_notes: Minor runtime improvements: lower streaming token emit latency via kernel scheduling, KV-cache coalescing, and adaptive batching flush/backpressure handling. Improvements are backwards-compatible; operators can configure adaptive flush behavior via streaming.flush.* runtime flags.
notes_on_rollback: No DB migrations. Rollback is safe by reverting the runtime binary; operator flags allow disabling adaptive flush if needed.
manual_steps_for_ops:
- Update runtime config: streaming.flush.adaptive_enabled=true (default)
- Optional tuning: streaming.flush.min_emit_ms=4, streaming.flush.max_batch_tokens=64
- Monitor metrics: runtime.emit_latency_p50/p95, runtime.emit_backpressure_events, runtime.kvcache_hit_rate
